name: Chris Brady
bio: Joined the Chicago Fire FC Academy in 2017 and signed his first professional homegrown contract on March 24, 2020 at age 16. Became Chicago's full-time starter in 2023 at age 19, the youngest opening-day goalkeeper in club history. Has tallied more than 300 saves and 25 clean sheets for the Fire in MLS regular season play. Named to MLS' '22 Under 22' list in three consecutive seasons (2023-25), the only goalkeeper recognized in 2025. Backed up Turner at the 2025 Concacaf Gold Cup as the U.S. reached the final. Recalled for the March 2026 friendlies vs. Belgium and Portugal, his fourth senior camp under Pochettino.

name: Matt Freese
bio: Son of the late Dr. Matthew Freese, a well-known orthopedic surgeon. Went through the Philadelphia Union youth academy before walking on to the Harvard Crimson soccer team. Went undrafted and signed with Philadelphia Union, becoming their starter. Joined New York City FC in 2023. Named NYCFC's Goalkeeper of the Year in consecutive seasons. Represented the United States at the U-19 and U-23 levels before earning his first senior cap in June 2025. Displaced Matt Turner as the USMNT starter for the 2025 Concacaf Gold Cup.

name: Matt Turner
bio: Son of Stu Turner and Cindy Turner; grew up in Park Ridge, N.J. Did not begin playing soccer until age 14, having previously focused on baseball and basketball. Walked on to the Fairfield University men's soccer team, recording 39 appearances and 21 shutouts. Went undrafted in the 2016 MLS SuperDraft and signed with New England Revolution after a successful preseason trial. Set a single-year USMNT record for a goalkeeper with 13 caps in 2021, including a penalty save on his debut. Earned MLS Goalkeeper of the Year in 2021 after posting 17 clean sheets in 33 matches. Transferred to Arsenal in 2022 for $10 million. Won the 2024 CONCACAF Nations League, contributing to the USMNT's third consecutive title. Named to the 2026 World Cup roster as the veteran starter option.

name: Max Arfsten
bio: Starred at San Joaquin Memorial High School in Fresno before attending UC Davis. Appeared in 39 matches as an Aggie, tallying nine goals and eight assists, earning Big West All-Freshman honors in 2019. Left UC Davis early to sign with the San Jose Earthquakes reserve team, then was selected by Columbus Crew in the 2023 MLS SuperDraft. Helped the Crew win the 2023 MLS Cup in his rookie season and the 2024 Leagues Cup. Named an MLS All-Star in 2025. Made his USMNT debut against Venezuela on Jan. 18, 2025. His five USMNT assists in 2025 were the most by any U.S. player in a calendar year since Jordan Morris in 2019. Scored his first senior international goal vs. Costa Rica at the 2025 Concacaf Gold Cup quarterfinals.

name: Sergiño Dest
bio: Born in Almere, Netherlands to an American father and Dutch mother, giving him dual nationality. Came through the Ajax youth academy, one of the world's most prestigious. Joined FC Barcelona in 2020 in a landmark move. Chose to represent the USA over the Netherlands after discussions with U.S. Soccer. Made his USMNT debut in October 2020 and quickly became a starter. Known for his speed, technical ability, and ability to play at both right back and left back. Was part of the USMNT squad that reached the Round of 16 at the 2022 FIFA World Cup.

name: Alex Freeman
bio: Born in Baltimore but raised in Plantation, Florida. Made his first MLS start for Orlando City SC just over a year before earning a World Cup spot. Moved to Villarreal CF in Spain, helping the club qualify for the UEFA Champions League. Made his USMNT debut in June 2025 vs. Turkey. One of the fastest rises in recent USMNT history — within 18 months went from first MLS start to 2026 World Cup roster. Nicknamed for his composure under pressure; his debut challenge defending against Kenan Yildiz was cited as proof he belonged at this level.

name: Mark McKenzie
bio: Born in New York City but grew up in Bear, Delaware. Came through the Philadelphia Union Academy and signed a homegrown contract. Moved to Belgian club KRC Genk in 2021 before joining Toulouse FC in France's Ligue 1. A versatile center back who can also play as a defensive midfielder. Made his USMNT debut in 2020. One of 13 dual nationals on the 2026 World Cup roster. Known for his composure on the ball and aerial ability. Part of the Toulouse squad that has established itself in Ligue 1 after earning promotion.

name: Tim Ream
bio: A cultured center back who displays good instincts and skill passing out of the back. Built his resume during eight seasons in England, earning Player of the Season awards at Bolton in 2013-14 and 2014-15 and with Fulham in 2017-18, helping the club to promotion to the English Premier League. Named USMNT captain ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. One of the most experienced players on the roster with 80 caps. Was part of the USMNT squad at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. Grew up in St. Louis, Missouri, before playing college soccer at Saint Louis University. Joined New York Red Bulls in 2010 before moving to Bolton Wanderers in England. Returned to MLS with Charlotte FC.

name: Chris Richards
bio: Full name is Chris Jeffrey Richards. Nicknamed 'Texas'. Signed with FC Dallas as a Homegrown Player on April 12, 2018. Joined Bayern Munich on Jan. 24, 2019. Appeared with the Bayern first team in all three of its International Champions Cup matches during summer 2018 against PSG, Juventus and Manchester City. Voted 2025 U.S. Soccer Male Player of the Year. Played basketball from 6th to 11th grade, earning all-area honors twice. Dad played professional basketball overseas, sister plays volleyball and brother plays soccer and basketball. Favorite soccer players are Jerome Boateng and Carles Puyol. Lists Michael Jordan as his biggest athletic inspiration. Proud owner of a dog named Zoe.

name: Antonee Robinson
bio: Named 2024 U.S. Soccer Male Player of the Year, becoming the first defender to earn the honor since Oguchi Onyewu in 2006. Son of American father Marlon Robinson, a former Duke University soccer standout (1981-84), and English mother Kelly. Holds dual U.S.-English nationality through his paternal grandmother's citizenship established in White Plains, N.Y. Grew up in Liverpool, England, immersed in American television, spending his childhood watching Disney Channel and Nickelodeon. Nickname 'Jedi' originated at age five when his father asked him to choose a famous soccer player as an idol — instead, he picked the name from his favorite childhood cartoon. Started all four matches at the 2022 FIFA World Cup, anchoring the left side of the USMNT defense. Part of three CONCACAF Nations League championships (2019, 2022, 2023).

name: Miles Robinson
bio: Grew up in Arlington, Massachusetts and attended Arlington High School. Played college soccer at Wake Forest University. Drafted by Atlanta United FC in 2019 and quickly became a starter, helping the club win the 2018 MLS Cup (while on loan) and the 2019 MLS Cup. Suffered a ruptured Achilles in 2022 but made a full comeback. Moved to FC Cincinnati in 2023, becoming a stalwart of the defense. Made his USMNT debut in 2020. Part of the squad that reached the Round of 16 at the 2022 World Cup. Known for his powerful aerial ability and composure in possession.

name: Joe Scally
bio: Grew up on Long Island, N.Y. with brother Drew, sister Ana, and parents Joe Scally and Margaret Peragine — herself a former soccer player. Attended Sachem North High School and played club soccer for various Long Island Junior Soccer League youth teams. Joined the New York City FC Academy at U-13 level in 2015. On March 21, 2018, at 15 years old, became just the second player from the NYCFC Academy to sign with the first team. In November 2019, NYCFC reached an agreement with Borussia Mönchengladbach for his transfer; he moved to Germany in January 2021. Made his Bundesliga debut just four days after his cup debut, in the season opener against Bayern Munich. Made 30 league appearances in his first Bundesliga season. Family owns The Village Idiot Pub in Long Island. Golfs frequently with best friend and USMNT teammate Gio Reyna.

name: Auston Trusty
bio: Born and raised in Media, Pennsylvania. Came through the Philadelphia Union Academy and signed a homegrown contract before moving to Colorado Rapids in MLS. Moved to Europe with Birmingham City in the Championship before joining Celtic FC in Scotland. Led Celtic to a dramatic comeback in the Scottish Premiership, helping the club hoist the domestic league trophy. Earned his first USMNT cap on March 24, 2023 vs. Grenada. One of the tallest outfield players on the World Cup roster at 6'3". Known for his dominant aerial presence and calm distribution from the back.

name: Tyler Adams
bio: The son of Melissa Russo, grew up in a single-parent household before she reconnected with old high school classmate and now step-dad, Darryl Sullivan. Has three step-brothers: Darryl Jr., Dylan and Donovan. Captained the USMNT nine times prior to the 2022 FIFA World Cup. First wore the armband in the 4-0 win against Costa Rica on June 9, 2021. His first international goal proved the game-winner in the 1-0 win against Mexico on Sept. 11, 2018 in Nashville. Became the first USMNT player to score in the UEFA Champions League quarterfinal with RB Leipzig vs. Atlético Madrid. Joined Leeds United for $24 million in 2022, then moved to AFC Bournemouth in the Premier League. Enjoys traveling — says Iceland is his favorite country. Interested in pursuing sports psychology once his playing career is finished.

name: Sebastian Berhalter
bio: Son of former USMNT head coach Gregg Berhalter and former UNC four-time NCAA champion Rosalind Berhalter. Born in London, England while his father was playing professionally in Europe. Made his USMNT debut on June 10, 2025 vs. Switzerland. One of 13 dual nationals on the 2026 World Cup roster. Plays as a box-to-box or attacking central midfielder. Developed through the New York City FC Academy before moving to the professional level. Signed with Vancouver Whitecaps FC, becoming a key contributor in MLS. Scored his first USMNT goal in just his second appearance.

name: Weston McKennie
bio: Scored in his USMNT debut, a 1-1 draw against reigning European champions Portugal on Nov. 14, 2017. Recorded the fastest hat trick from the start of a USMNT match, scoring three goals in 13 minutes vs. Cuba in 2019. Won U.S. Soccer's Male Player of the Year in 2020. Headed home a late equalizer to send the inaugural Concacaf Nations League Final against Mexico to extra time — the USMNT won 3-2 and McKennie earned Player of the Tournament. Joined Juventus in August 2020; became the first U.S. international to play in and win the Coppa Italia. Began playing soccer near Kaiserslautern, Germany, while his father served in the U.S. Army at Ramstein Air Base. Fluent in German with proficiency in Italian and Spanish. Said meeting Landon Donovan and Carlos Bocanegra during the U.S. team's visit to Ramstein Air Base in 2006 was when he first realized he could play for the U.S. internationally. Learned to play piano through YouTube. Is a big Harry Potter fan and often celebrates goals in tribute to the series.

name: Gio Reyna
bio: Full name is Giovanni Alejandro Reyna. His father Claudio earned 112 caps with the USMNT and captained the squad at the 2002 and 2006 World Cups. His mother Danielle played for the USWNT and won four national championships at the University of North Carolina. With Gio's debut on Nov. 12, 2020, the Reynas became the first family to have a father, son and child all appear for U.S. Soccer's senior national teams. Named after Giovanni van Bronckhorst. At 17 years and 350 days, became the youngest American to start in the UEFA Champions League in Dortmund's 2-0 win against Zenit St. Petersburg. Became the youngest player in Bundesliga history to make 50 league appearances. Voted the 2020 U.S. Young Male Player of the Year. Scored his first USMNT goal in a 6-2 win against Panama on Nov. 16, 2020 — at 18 years, 3 days, the third youngest goal scorer in USMNT history. Proud parent of a cat named Swag. Golfs frequently with best friend and USMNT teammate Joe Scally.

name: Cristian Roldan
bio: Made his USMNT debut on July 12, 2017 in a 3-2 win over Martinique at the Concacaf Gold Cup. Helped the USA claim the Concacaf Gold Cup championship in 2017 and 2021. Has appeared in over 250 games since 2015 for the Seattle Sounders. In May 2022, helped Seattle become the first MLS team to win the Concacaf Champions League. Named captain of the 2021 MLS All-Star Team. Helped Seattle to four MLS Cup finals, winning in 2016 and 2019. Grew up in Pico Rivera, California, where he attended El Rancho High School. Led his school to a state championship and was honored as the 2013 National High School Player of the Year after scoring 54 goals and adding 31 assists. Older brother Cesar is head athletic trainer for the LA Galaxy; younger brother Alex is his Seattle Sounders teammate. Father is from Guatemala and mother from El Salvador — while Cristian plays for the USA, Alex plays internationally for El Salvador. On April 5, 2022, partnered with the City of Pico Rivera to open a futsal mini-soccer field in his hometown.

name: Malik Tillman
bio: Born in Nuremberg, Germany to an American father, giving him dual nationality. Came through the Bayern Munich youth academy, one of the most prestigious in Europe. Made his professional debut with Bayern Munich's senior team before moving to Rangers FC in Scotland on loan. Scored an impressive 13 goals in 33 appearances for Rangers. Committed to representing the United States over Germany. Made his USMNT debut in 2022. Versatile and skillful both as an attacking central midfielder and as a winger — Pochettino relied on him heavily in starting lineups leading up to the 2026 World Cup. Moved to PSV Eindhoven and then Bayer 04 Leverkusen, becoming a key contributor in the Bundesliga.

name: Brenden Aaronson
bio: The son of Rusty and Jannell Aaronson; younger brother Paxten also plays professionally for the Philadelphia Union. Made his USMNT debut at age 19 in the 1-0 win against Costa Rica on Feb. 1, 2020. With four goals and three assists, led all USMNT players with seven goal contributions in 2021. Joined Red Bull Salzburg in January 2021, recording nine goals and nine assists in 45 league matches and helping the club to back-to-back Austrian League and Cup doubles. Joined Leeds United for $30 million in May 2022 — scored his first Leeds goal in a 3-0 win against Chelsea. Growing up, admired Lionel Messi and Steven Gerrard. Describes himself as a huge gamer, spending time playing FIFA, Fortnite and Rocket League. His ideal day off is a day at the Jersey Shore.

name: Folarin Balogun
bio: Born in Brooklyn, New York but raised in London, England, holding dual U.S.-British nationality. Came through the Arsenal youth academy and signed his first professional contract with the Gunners. Had a breakthrough loan season at Reims in Ligue 1, scoring 21 goals and earning a move to AS Monaco. Made his USMNT debut on June 15, 2023 vs. Mexico — one of 13 dual nationals on the 2026 World Cup roster. Chose to represent the United States over England. Known for his intelligent movement, quick acceleration, and composed finishing in the penalty area. One of three pure strikers on Pochettino's 2026 World Cup squad.

name: Ricardo Pepi
bio: Named 2021 U.S. Soccer Young Male Player of the Year. Made his USMNT debut on September 8, 2021 in a 4-1 World Cup Qualifying win at Honduras — involved in all four goals, scoring the game-winner and adding two assists. At 18 years and 242 days, became the second youngest player to appear for the USMNT in a World Cup Qualifier. Led FC Dallas with 13 goals in 2021 and earned 2021 MLS Young Player of the Year honors. Transferred to FC Augsburg in January 2022 for a reported $20 million — the most for a homegrown MLS player in history at the time. Grew up in a Spanish-speaking household; mother born in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, father born in El Paso. Eligible to represent both the USA and Mexico — chose the USMNT in August 2021. Enjoys drawing and sketching in his free time.

name: Christian Pulisic
bio: Born and raised in Hershey, Pennsylvania. Parents Mark and Kelley Pulisic both played college soccer at George Mason University; father also played professional indoor soccer with the Harrisburg Heat. At age seven, moved to Tackley, England for a year while his mother was on a teaching exchange, beginning his soccer journey at Brackley Town. Came up through PA Classics in Pennsylvania before joining Borussia Dortmund at age 15. Made his Dortmund debut at 17, becoming the youngest American to start in the Bundesliga. Nicknamed 'Captain America.' Holds Croatian citizenship through his paternal grandfather — middle name Mate is a tribute to his grandfather. Also tied with Landon Donovan for four U.S. Player of the Year awards. Most experienced player on the 2026 World Cup roster with 84 caps. Scored a goal and added an assist at the 2022 World Cup. His childhood soccer idol was Luís Figo.

name: Tim Weah
bio: Born in Brooklyn, New York to Liberian father and world soccer legend George Weah and Jamaican mother Clar. George Weah won the 1995 Ballon d'Or — the first African player to win the award. Scored his first international goal in his second USMNT appearance, tallying in the 3-0 win against Bolivia on May 28, 2018 — the fifth youngest goal scorer in team history. Made his U.S. debut on March 27, 2018 at age 18, becoming the first player born in 2000 to play for the USMNT. Scored a hat trick in the 5-0 win against Paraguay at the 2017 U-17 FIFA World Cup — the first U.S. player at any level to score a hat trick in the knockout stage of a World Cup. Won two Ligue 1 titles with PSG and Lille. Also eligible to play for France, Jamaica and Liberia — chose to represent the United States. A talented music producer who makes rap, hip hop and soul music in his free time. Big fan of fashion.

name: Haji Wright
bio: Born in Los Angeles, California to a father from Ghana and a mother from Liberia. Has three siblings, including brother Hanif, who is also a soccer player. Cousin is former NFL running back Joseph Addai, who won Super Bowl XLI with the Indianapolis Colts. Began his European career at Schalke 04 before stints at VVV-Venlo, SønderjyskE, and Antalyaspor. Joined Coventry City in August 2023. Led the EFL Championship in goals during the 2025-26 season with 17 goals through April 2026, helping Coventry City secure promotion to the Premier League on May 4, 2026. Set the EFL record for most goals in a single season by a U.S.-born player. Returned from Achilles rehabilitation in October 2025 and scored twice vs. Australia. Married wife Jana in June 2025 in a ceremony in California.

name: Alejandro Zendejas
bio: The son of Alfredo Zendejas and Mónica Saavedra, with older siblings Ana Lucía and Alfredo Jr. Born in Chihuahua, Mexico but raised in Texas; a dual national who committed to representing the United States over Mexico in March 2023. Made his USMNT debut on Jan. 25, 2023 vs. Serbia. Plays as a winger for Club América in Mexico's Liga MX. Was a surprise inclusion to the 2026 World Cup roster after limited minutes under Pochettino earlier in the cycle — his last appearance before the announcement had been in September 2025. Reacted with shock and tears when informed he made the World Cup squad: 'I couldn't believe it. I was just super in shock, grateful.' Known for his dribbling ability, pace, and direct play on the wing.
